header:
**$100 a month** at 7%.
What's it worth in 40 years?
footer: 7% a year, compounded monthly · not a forecast

vo.text: Year 20: about $52,093. **More growth than you put in.**
You put in $48,000. **It's worth over 5 times that.**

notes: Maths: $100 deposited at each month-end, 7%/12 a month, compounded monthly. Worth after n months = 100 × ((1 + 0.07/12)^n − 1) ÷ (0.07/12). Year 1 (n = 12) = $1,239.26; year 5 = $7,159.29; year 10 = $17,308.48; year 20 = $52,092.67; year 30 = $121,997.10; year 40 = $262,481.34. You put in = $100 × 12 × years. Growth passes what you put in during year 19 (month 217): at year 20 growth is $28,092.67 > $24,000 put in. $262,481.34 ÷ $48,000 = 5.47, so 'over 5 times'. 7% is a stated assumption (roughly the S&P 500's long-run return after inflation), not a forecast; no fees or taxes.
